# Nvidia quarterly sales are expected to nearly double to about $109 billion

Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday after the close, with Wall Street looking for sales just above the company's $108 billion outlook.

By Opening Bell Daily Staff

Nov 13, 2026

Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday after the close, with Wall Street looking for about $109 billion in quarterly sales. [...] That would be nearly double the $57.0 billion the company recorded a year earlier, and up 13% from the $96.2 billion it posted in the July quarter.

The estimate sits just above the $108 billion midpoint Nvidia guided to in August, and inside its plus or minus 2% range. Analysts also look for adjusted earnings of about $2.48 a share, up from $2.22 last quarter and well above the $1.30 Nvidia earned a year ago.

results.content:
Huang then announced Agile ONE SN, a reference humanoid built on Isaac GR00T — a 31-degree-of-freedom body, expected to be available next year, designed to cut researcher setup time from weeks to days. 

The platform is modular: researchers can use the full workflow or pull in selected components.   
 “This is a great starting point,” Huang said. [...] Huang closed by discussing RTX Spark laptops, which launched last week, bringing together RTX graphics and NVIDIA’s full-stack AI platform in slim, premium Windows PCs for accelerated creation, immersive gaming and powerful local AI. 

He compared its 1 petaflop of performance and 128GB of memory with the DGX-1 he delivered to OpenAI in 2016 — then made the difference in size the punchline: [...] “This now represents the breadth of technology necessary to create the AI factory,” Huang said. “This is what NVIDIA builds today, and this is the foundation by which we can enable Europe to be part of the AI ecosystem, the AI economy.”    
   
 He said Vera Rubin, in full production, extends NVIDIA’s computing platform beyond models and large language models to process the entire AI agent. He also showed several of NVIDIA’s latest rack-scale hardware offerings.

# Nvidia quarterly sales are expected to nearly double to about $109 billion

Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday after the close, with Wall Street looking for sales just above the company's $108 billion outlook.

By Opening Bell Daily Staff

Nov 13, 2026

Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday after the close, with Wall Street looking for about $109 billion in quarterly sales. [...] That would be nearly double the $57.0 billion the company recorded a year earlier, and up 13% from the $96.2 billion it posted in the July quarter.

The estimate sits just above the $108 billion midpoint Nvidia guided to in August, and inside its plus or minus 2% range. Analysts also look for adjusted earnings of about $2.48 a share, up from $2.22 last quarter and well above the $1.30 Nvidia earned a year ago.

## Recent developments
- **CEO Transition and Resignation:** Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA CEO on November 12, 2026, following revelations regarding an independent board investigation into personal relationships with business executives, including one linked to a foreign intelligence effort [1, 4, 5]. Colette Kress, EVP and CFO, was appointed interim CEO, and Harvey C. Jones was named the first-ever Chair of the Board [1].
- **Executive Leadership Scrutiny:** Investigations by the board revealed relationships involving Huang and corporate personnel, prompting his departure and an ongoing internal review [4, 5].
- **Product & Infrastructure Announcements:** Prior to the leadership shakeup, NVIDIA announced major expansions at GTC Berlin in October 2026, including the Vera Rubin platform deployments, DSX POD AI factories for Europe, and the OpenShell reference architecture for safe AI agents [11, 12, 14].

## Talking points
- **Interim Leadership Stability:** Address how interim CEO Colette Kress and the executive team plan to maintain operational continuity, financial performance, and customer trust during the search for a permanent CEO.
- **Corporate Governance & Compliance:** Discuss the steps NVIDIA is taking to reinforce governance, internal controls, and security protocols following the board investigation.
- **AI Infrastructure & Vera Rubin Momentum:** Reiterate strong ongoing demand for the next-generation Vera Rubin architecture, cloud partnerships (such as Oracle and AWS), and multi-gigawatt data center rollouts [10, 13].

## Open questions
- Who is leading the search for a permanent CEO, and what is the expected timeline for an appointment?
- How will the independent investigation impact NVIDIA’s government relations, compliance audits, or international market access?
- Will the leadership transition affect the projected fiscal timelines for the Vera Rubin platform and upcoming fiscal 2028 guidance?
